n: God speaks to those seeking righteousness: remember the rock you were cut from and the quarry you were dug out of—your spiritual ancestors. Jacob quotes this chapter as 2 Nephi 8.

f.w: look unto the rock whence ye are hewn
hewn
f.g: Cut, carved out (as stone from a quarry).

n: Look to Abraham and Sarah. God called Abraham when he was just one man and multiplied him into a nation. If God did that, He can restore a small remnant now.

f.w: Abraham your father
Sarah that bare you

n: The Lord will comfort Zion and turn her ruins into a garden like Eden, full of joy, thanksgiving, and music.

f.w: he will make her wilderness like Eden

n: Listen, My people: law and justice will go out from Me as a light to the nations.

f.w: a law shall proceed from me

n: God’s righteousness and salvation are near and already on the way. Distant lands will hope in His arm—His saving power.

f.w: on mine arm shall they trust

n: The sky will vanish like smoke and the earth wear out like clothing, but God’s salvation lasts forever.

f.w: the heavens shall vanish away like smoke

n: You who have God’s law in your heart: don’t fear people’s scorn or insults. 2 Nephi 8:7 is the same.

f.w: the people in whose heart is my law
fear ye not the reproach of men

n: Those mockers will be eaten like moth-eaten wool, but God’s righteousness and salvation will last for all generations.
Now the people cry out: wake up, Arm of the Lord, as in ancient days! You defeated Rahab and the sea monster—poetic names for chaos and for Egypt.

f.w: Rahab
f.g: Not Rahab of Jericho; a mythic sea monster symbolizing chaos, used poetically for Egypt.

f.w: the dragon

n: You dried up the sea and made a road through the depths for the redeemed to cross—the Exodus through the Red Sea.

f.w: made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over

n: So the redeemed will return to Zion singing, crowned with everlasting joy, while sorrow and mourning run away. Nearly identical to Isaiah 35:10.

f.w: the redeemed of the LORD shall return

n: God answers: I am the One who comforts you. Why fear mortal men who wither like grass?

f.w: I, even I, am he that comforteth you
a man that shall die

n: Why forget your Maker who spread out the heavens, and live in constant fear of the oppressor? Where is his fury now? It is gone.

f.w: where is the fury of the oppressor?

n: The bowed-down captive will soon be freed—he won’t die in the dungeon or go without bread.

f.w: The captive exile
f.g: Literally “the one bent over”—a prisoner stooped under chains.

n: For I am the Lord your God, who stirs up the sea so its waves roar; the Lord of Hosts is My name.

f.w: that divided the sea
f.g: Or “who stirs up the sea”; either way, God controls the waters.

n: God puts His words in His people’s mouth and shelters them in His hand, in order to establish a new heaven and earth and say to Zion, “You are My people.”

f.w: I have put my words in thy mouth
the shadow of mine hand

n: Wake up, Jerusalem! You drank God’s cup of wrath down to the dregs. In scripture, a cup can stand for one’s appointed suffering—Christ later drank the bitter cup for us.

f.w: the cup of his fury
dregs
f.g: The bitter sediment at the bottom of a cup.

n: Like a mother too drunk to stand, Jerusalem has no son to take her hand and guide her home.
Two calamities hit her—ruin and destruction, famine and sword. Who can comfort her? In 2 Nephi 8:19 this reads “These two sons are come unto thee,” suggesting two helpers.

f.w: These two things are come unto thee

n: Her sons lie collapsed in the streets like an antelope caught in a net, overcome by God’s anger. 2 Nephi 8:20 adds “save these two”—many Latter-day Saints connect these to the two prophets in Jerusalem in Revelation 11.

f.w: Thy sons have fainted
wild bull

n: So listen, afflicted Jerusalem, staggering—not from wine but from suffering.

f.w: drunken, but not with wine

n: The Lord who defends His people takes the cup of staggering from her hand—she will never drink it again. Judgment gives way to mercy.

f.w: that pleadeth the cause of his people
f.g: Who argues His people’s case like a defense lawyer.

f.w: thou shalt no more drink it again

n: God will give that cup to her tormentors, who forced her to lie down so they could walk over her back like a road. Ancient conquerors sometimes literally walked on defeated foes. 2 Nephi 8 continues into Isaiah 52:1-2.

f.w: Bow down, that we may go over
